text: A predictive project has an agreed scope for a library booking system. A librarian requests an additional reporting feature. Before promising delivery, what should the project manager do?

options.text: Reject every change once the project starts.
Ask developers to hide the work inside another task.
Record the request and assess its effects on the project constraints and risks.

text: A design change has been analysed and would alter an approved baseline. The project plan assigns this decision to a review board, but the requester wants work to begin today. What is the appropriate next step?

options.text: Implement now and ask for approval at the next meeting.
Submit the assessed request to the designated board and obtain its decision before implementation.
Let the most available developer approve it.
Delete the baseline so that approval is no longer needed.

text: The designated authority approves a scope change and its revised delivery date. How should the manager make the decision usable by the team?

options.text: Keep the approval in a private inbox until the end of the project.
Leave the old plan in place and tell people to remember the new date.
Update the affected controlled records, communicate the decision and track the approved work.
Treat approval as evidence that the work is already complete.
